claims.text: Machine-learning-assisted high-throughput screening can rapidly identify promising RHEA compositions.
The identified RHEA compositions can simultaneously possess high intrinsic strength, good ductility, and low weight.
Machine-learning-assisted screening is faster and more screening-efficient than traditional thermo-kinetic or brute-force simulation methods.
Multi-principal refractory alloy systems typically form disordered BCC or related solid solutions.
The proposed machine-learning model is trained on existing experimental and computational data.
The model can predict and screen the full RHEA compositional space for desired mechanical properties.
Candidate alloys should be validated by mechanical testing at room and elevated temperatures relevant to high-temperature applications.
Arc melting or mechanical alloying can be used as conventional processing routes for the proposed candidates.
Predicted microstructure and phase stability mediate the balance between strength and ductility.
Severe lattice distortion within a BCC solid solution provides a balance of strength and ductility.
The proposed microstructural state also reduces alloy density.
Machine learning can integrate heterogeneous experimental and simulation data for alloy design.
The machine-learning model can capture atomic-size mismatch, mixing enthalpy, and entropic contributions.
Atomic-size mismatch, mixing enthalpy, and entropic contributions govern microstructure formation, phase stability, and mechanical response.
The framework will identify compositions with improved intrinsic strength and ductility and reduced density.
Thermo-kinetic analysis and high-throughput CALPHAD screening are computationally expensive and slow because of the size of HEA composition spaces.
Predictions are less reliable in compositional regions poorly represented by the training data.
The model may not fully capture oxidation behavior.
The model may not fully capture processing-induced microstructural evolution.
Failure to reproduce predicted properties within approximately 20%, or failure to realize the predicted phases, would falsify the claimed reliability of the screening method.
